newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BEKAERT SAYS 1996 PROFIT TO RISE DUE TO BMA.
newsitem.headline: BEKAERT SAYS 1996 PROFIT TO RISE DUE TO BMA.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV reported on Wednesday a 25 percent drop in group net profit for the first six months of 1996 but said profit for the year would rise thanks to the sale of shares in Japanese subsidiary Bridgestone Metalpha Corp.

"Consolidated profit for the full year 1996 will be substantially higher than in 1995 due to a capital gain of 2.2 billion Belgian francs on the sale of 10.1 million BMA shares sold in July," Bekaert said in a statement on earnings in the year to June 30.
Bekaert said a worse-than-expected slump in demand for its products in Europe squeezed margins, leaving group net profit for the period 25 percent lower at 1.27 billion Belgian francs.
Sales rose three percent to 32.94 billion Belgian francs, but on a comparable basis slipped nearly four percent, Bekaert said. Gross margin on sales fell to 11.8 from 13.8 percent.
"For the current operations Bekaert does not expect any significant improvement in profitability for the second half of the year," the company said.
Bekaert said in July it expected current earnings to be about 15 percent down on 1995's 3.0 billion Belgian francs.
